subject: Access delivery handoff: SSO/SCIM, service accounts, and org policies for Helix Bank
messages:
From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@helixbank.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@helixbank.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Access delivery handoff: next steps

Thanks team — excited to get this moving. Quick summary of Helix priorities so we can align the handoff:

- SSO/SAML: Our identity team requires IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows; we'd like metadata and ACS endpoints for both.
- SCIM: We only want to provision groups under the "Redwood-Apps" OU, with delta sync every 5 minutes if possible.
- IP allowlists: We will publish a stable egress range; during rollout we'll use a temporary CIDR range (attached).
- Service accounts: We need a pattern for least-privilege service accounts for model calls and for ingestion pipelines.
- Org policies: Audit log retention and key rotation cadence are non-negotiable for us (SOC2 requirement).

Can you confirm who at Redwood will own each bullet and a realistic timeline? Also attaching our SSO metadata and the current allowlist.

Attachments: helix_sso_metadata.xml, network_allowlist.csv

Thanks,
Emily Hart
Director, Cloud Security
Helix Bank

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@helixbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access delivery handoff: next steps

Hi Emily — thank you for the clear list. TL;DR: I'll coordinate the program and own the timeline; Marissa will manage the CS/ops scheduling; Karthik will own SCIM and service-account guardrails. Proposed plan below.

Planned owners & targets:
- SSO/SAML (jonas): provide SP metadata, test endpoints for IdP and SP flows, target: 3 business days for test endpoints, 7 business days for production metadata.
- SCIM (karthik): scoping matrix + provisioning rules, initial delta sync in staging in 5-7 business days.
- IP allowlists (marissa): confirm temporary CIDR during rollout, validate egress ranges with infra, coordinate firewall change window — target 4 business days.
- Service accounts & least privilege (karthik + security): runbook and example IAM policies, draft in 5 business days.
- Org policies / audit logs (laura): confirm retention SLAs and key rotation docs — separate compliance packet in 6 business days.

I'll assemble a shared checklist in the Drive link and propose a three-phase rollout: 1) staging validation (IDP & SCIM), 2) controlled production cutover (IP allowlist window), 3) post-cutover audit and policy handoff.

Next steps: Marissa, can you propose 2x 45-minute windows for a technical handshake this week? Karthik, please review Emily's SCIM group scope in the attached matrix and flag any API gaps.

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@helixbank.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

1) SAML metadata exchange and test accounts (15m)
2) SCIM scoping & rate limits (15m)

4) IP allowlist timing and rollback plan (5m)

I'll include the runbook doc and a quick checklist in the Drive link before the call.

Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emily Hart <emily.hart@helixbank.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Access delivery handoff: SCIM delta sync question

Emily — quick technical note after reviewing your scim_scope_matrix.xlsx:

- SCIM filtering: We support group filtering by attribute and OU, but our current SCIM server implements incremental sync via the list/changes endpoint (not RFC 7644 "sync"). For delta every 5 minutes we'll do a polling approach; recommend rate limit of 120 requests/min per customer to avoid throttling.
- Group membership mapping: we need a primaryGroup attribute (we can map Helix's "Security-Apps" membership to Redwood team IDs). Please confirm if you can expose group IDs consistently.
- Service accounts: we'll create two patterns — one short-lived token for ingestion with narrow scopes (ingest:write) and one longer-lived machine-to-machine credential scoped to model:invoke with rate limits. Draft IAM snippets attached.

Action items for Helix before the handshake:
1) confirm group ID consistency (Emily)
2) confirm whether IdP-initiated SSO will be enabled for test users
3) provide contact for firewall team to coordinate allowlist windows

I'll bring the SCIM test harness and example curl commands to the call.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@helixbank.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Singh <rajesh.singh@helixbank.com>, Helix Bank Security <security@helixbank.com>

Subject: Re: Access delivery handoff: confirmation for Thursday handshake

Thanks Karthik — we can expose stable group IDs. Rajesh will join the call as our SCIM owner. Firewall contact is "ops-firewall@helixbank.com" (cc'd on this thread). Thursday 7/8 is a bit tight for our team; can we do Friday 7/9 at 14:00 PT instead?

Also, Helix Security needs a short evidence bundle for your audit controls before production cutover:
- proof of audit log retention (90 days),
- key rotation policy (KMS logs),
- a Red Team contact for incident response.

I attached an initial scim_scope_matrix.xlsx with expected groups and a note column. We'll upload the formal evidence to the Drive link after the handshake.

Attachments: scim_scope_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Emily Hart
Director, Cloud Security
Helix Bank

- We'll present SSO metadata and run the IdP-initiated login flow in staging.

Please ensure your firewall team contact (ops-firewall@helixbank.com) is on the call. If anything changes, flag it ASAP. Looking forward to the handshake.

Laura Bennett
